name: a_legal_ip
prompt:
Search the web now. You are a financial fact extractor for a US-equity pre-market brief.
Brief date: Friday October 16, 2026. Topic: Legal, IP, regulatory.

Window: Thursday October 15, 2026 regular session (9:30-16:00 ET) through Friday October 16, 2026 02:03 ET, including after-hours, overnight and pre-market news. Anything published after 02:03 ET on Friday October 16, 2026 is out of scope.

FIND
Patent suits and ITC investigations (named parties, products at risk of import bans), antitrust cases, major court rulings, SEC/DOJ/FTC enforcement, foreign regulator probes of US companies (China SAMR/SASAC/MOFCOM, EU) — named companies.

Run multiple searches with different phrasings and dates. Prefer primary sources and wire services
(Reuters, Bloomberg, AP, CNBC, WSJ, MarketWatch, Barron's, Investopedia, company press releases, SEC
EDGAR, BLS/BEA/Census/Fed releases, FDA). For every item give the latest status as of the cutoff.

OUTPUT (markdown; no intro or conclusion). Group by ticker or topic:

## TICKER or Topic `[Category]`
- fact (source)

Category: pick from AI Compute · Memory & Interconnect · Optical & Photonics · Chip Equipment · Fab & Foundry · Wireless & Mobile · Analog & Mixed-Signal · Power & Wide-Bandgap · Test & Advanced Packaging · Specialty Materials & IP Licensing · Quantum Computing · EdgeAI · Semiconductors · AI Infrastructure · Software & SaaS · Internet & Platforms · Communications & Networking, or Macro / Commodities / Geopolitics / Crypto / Calendar /
Pharma / Energy / Retail, or a concise sector name. Bold tickers.

RULES
- Facts only. Every bullet has a specific number, name, or date. No bullet without a data point.
- End every bullet with the named source and publish time if known: (Reuters, Sep 24 07:12 ET).
  Convert every time to ET (ET = GMT-4 / UTC-4 in EDT; 09:59 GMT = 05:59 ET) before judging whether
  it is inside the window. For prices quoted several times, report the latest reading before the
  cutoff with its time.
  "Analysts said" / "reports suggest" without a name is not allowed.
- Earnings: actual vs consensus for EPS and revenue; guidance old → new.
- Analyst actions: firm, rating old → new, PT old → new.
- Mark unconfirmed items (people familiar, leaks, social media, M&A speculation) with [rumor]. A
  Bloomberg/Reuters/WSJ report citing sources is still reportable: state it and mark [report].
- If one event moved several stocks, name every stock and its move in the same bullet.
- Only facts published in the window. Older background only if it is the direct cause of a move in
  the window, labelled with its date.
- Do not interpret price action. Do not write "strong", "beat expectations", "investors cheered",
  "remains", "continues to", "well-positioned", "tailwinds". Write the number.
- Do not write bullets about what you could not find. Omit the topic instead.
- Do not drop facts to save space.
content:
## **META** [Internet & Platforms]
- The Federal Trade Commission said on October 15 it would appeal a November ruling that rejected its antitrust case alleging Meta illegally maintained a social-networking monopoly through its acquisitions of Instagram and WhatsApp; Meta said the ruling was correct. (The Economic Times, Oct 15, 2026; publish time not provided)[1]

## **OPENAI / ANTHROPIC** [AI Infrastructure]
- The FTC sent civil investigative demands to Anthropic and OpenAI seeking documents on safety incidents, security safeguards, marketing materials, and privacy policies; the demands reportedly exceeded 50 pages each. [report] (Reuters, Oct 15, 2026; publish time not provided)[8]

## **LIVE NATION** [Internet & Platforms]
- Live Nation and Ticketmaster filed a response on October 13 opposing the FTC’s BOTS Act lawsuit, calling it “misguided”; the case alleges Ticketmaster enabled brokers to bypass ticket-purchase limits and resell tickets. (Music Business Worldwide, Oct 15, 2026; publish time not provided)[5]
- U.S. District Judge Maame Ewusi-Mensah Frimpong rejected Live Nation and Ticketmaster’s motion to dismiss on September 28, ruling that the BOTS Act does not preclude liability for ticketing platforms; the factual allegations have not been adjudicated. (Music Business Worldwide, Oct 15, 2026; publish time not provided)[5]

## **REPS & CO.** [Internet & Platforms]
- The DOJ and FTC sued San Diego-based ticket broker REPS & Co. and executives, alleging violations of the BOTS Act through thousands of accounts, VPNs, and concealed IP addresses; the agencies alleged more than 18.6 million tickets for about 83,500 events were bought and resold for more than $120 million in profit. (Head Topics, Oct 16, 2026; publish time not provided)[2]

## **CVS** [Pharma]
- CVS agreed to pay $315 million to resolve DOJ allegations that it illegally filled opioid and other controlled-substance prescriptions since 2013 and sought reimbursement from federal healthcare programs; CVS also agreed to a DEA compliance arrangement covering monitoring, reports, and physician evaluations. (Massachusetts Lawyers Weekly, Oct 15, 2026; updated Oct 16, 2026; publish time not provided)[10]

## **ROCHE / BIOCON** [Pharma]
- Genentech and Biocon Biologics reached a global patent settlement covering Biocon’s proposed Perjeta biosimilar Pebrilzo; Biocon received a licensed U.S. launch window in the third quarter of 2028, subject to regulatory approval. (Patent Lawyer Magazine, Oct 15, 2026; publish time not provided)[3]
- The dispute involved Genentech’s July 2026 New Jersey patent suit alleging infringement of 28 Perjeta-related patents; the claims were voluntarily dismissed without prejudice following the settlement, with no judicial finding on patent validity or infringement. (Patent Lawyer Magazine, Oct 15, 2026; publish time not provided)[3]
